Both Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic were preparing for war, and multiple uprisings against the Alliance have sprung throughout the galaxy.<ref name="KOTETChapter9" /> Theron identified several potential threats, assembling teams to neutralize [[White Maw]] forge-master [[Droub]] on Hoth,<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|Uprising: Firefrost}}</ref> rogue Coruscant Security Force Commander [[Kallin]] on Coruscant<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|Uprising: Divided We Fall}}</ref> and [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Alirra Semhess]]'s research into [[RAK-5 serum]] on the [[X7-Cratus]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]].<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|Uprising: Trial and Error}}</ref>

===The Order of Zildrog===
====Setting a trap on Iokath====
{{Quote|I heard rumors about the Order of Zildrog through my old underworld contacts. It took me months to even find them--and the whole time they were watching us. By the time I learned the truth about Zildrog, it was almost too late. They'd learned too much. I had to slow them down long enough for the Alliance to catch up. I had to join them--work from the inside.|Theron Shan|<ref name="Nathema">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|The Nathema Conspiracy}}</ref>}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_delivers_report.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan informs the Commander about the events on Iokath.]]
Through his old underworld contacts, Theron Shan heard rumours about the secretive [[Order of Zildrog]], which was behind the recent uprisings, but was unable to share his findings with anyone because the Alliance was under constant surveillance by [[GEMINI 16]], a rogue unit who worked with the Order. On his own, Theron searched for the Order for months and eventually contacted its leader [[Vinn Atrius]] under the guise of wanting to join the Order and bring down the very Alliance he helped build. Atrius refused to listen to Shan, which led Theron to arrange a trap for the Commander to prove his dedication.<ref name="Nathema" /> By this point the radiation levels on Iokath had subsided, and Theron leaked the location of another superweapon on it to the Eternal Alliance, Sith Empire and Galactic Republic simultaneously, with all three parties showing interest in it. Lana led a team to claim the weapon for the Alliance, while Theron stayed behind on Odessen and presented to Commander a report on the political standing of the Eternal Alliance. They received Lana's status report from Iokath, which was interrupted by the arrival of Imperial and Republic forces, who engaged each other. Lana and her team escaped notice and retreated to the [[Fleet Spire]], where they established an Alliance foothold, while the Commander summoned the Eternal Fleet to Iokath and departed there along with Theron.<ref name="The Forgotten World">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Forgotten World|Iokath}}</ref>

[[File:Theron_Shan_11.png|thumb|left|250px|Theron returns to Iokath.]]
When the Eternal Fleet dropped out of hyperspace, the Imperial and Republic fleets have not yet engaged each other, and a signal from the planet's surface broke the connection between the Eternal Throne and the Eternal Fleet, leaving the it dormant while the GEMINI captains looked for a workaround. Theron suggested to look for the source of the transmission on Iokath, proceeding with the Commander towards the surface in a Zakuul starfighter. They met Lana at the Fleet Spide, where she had apprehended Republic [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Elara Dorne]] and Imperial Major [[Malavai Quinn]], who had been sent by Supreme Commander Malcom and Darth Acina respectively to negotiate with the Alliance. Malcom who was angry at Theron for abandoning the Republic and siding with the Alliance, and both sides laid their claims to the superweapon and urged the Commander to ally with them against their enemy. Theron advised the Commander to ally with the Republic, but supported their decision regardless.<ref name="The Forgotten World" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Jace_Malcom.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan talks to his father, Jace Malcom.]]
As soon as the choice of allegiance was made with one faction, the other immediately launched a retaliatory strike, marking the beginning of the [[War on Iokath]]. Theron joined the Commander in defense of their position and later ventured into a nearby weapons cache to retrieve Iokath weapons and knowledge on how to use them.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Shots Fired|Iokath}}</ref> While downloading the files from an ancient console, Theron learned that the superweapon was powerful enough to wipe out all organic life on Iokath in distant past, in addition to ten trillion lives on other planets. They then returned to Lana, who discovered that the information of their new ally matched the data received by the Alliance and concluded that an outside party was behind the current events, and rightfully suspecting a traitor in their ranks.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Lost Arsenal|Iokath}}</ref>

[[File:Theron_Shan_during_War_on_Iokath.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan during the War on Iokath]]
Meanwhile, the Alliance's enemy used the schematics they received to engineer a backdoor access to the superweapon. Their leader contacted the Alliance, taunting them about their inevitable victory, despite the repeated warnings about the danger of the superweapon. Theron and Commander boarded a walker and stormed their enemy's base to stop the superweapon activation but were too late. The opposing faction's leader assumed the throne, awakening the legendary [[Six Gods|Old Gods]]. The resulting energy surge mortally wounded them, but also disabled the signal that kept the Eternal Fleet ships in lockdown. The Commander rushed towards the superweapon complex while Theron stayed behind to delay its full activation. Inside the complex the Commander assumed another throne and faced [[Tyth]], the first of Six Gods, just as a member of the Order sabotaged the throne. The Commander was brought to Fleet Spire to recuperate, where they discussed with Lana and Theron the best possible way to locate the traitor in their ranks. With no way to narrow down the list of suspects, Lana asked the Commander to approve full-time surveillance on the Eternal Alliance and its allies by an independent party, to which Theron strongly opposed, though he still promised to Commander that they would find the traitor.<ref name="Showdown">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Showdown on Iokath|Iokath}}</ref>

====Revelations on Umbara====
{{Quote|Ever since you defeated Valkorion, everything I've done has been towards one goal... The total destruction of the Eternal Alliance.|Theron fakes disillusionment in the Alliance|<ref name="Umbara" />}}
[[File:Theron_the_Traitor.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron leads the Commander and Lana into his trap.]]
After the events on Iokath, Theron contacted Vinn Atrius again, insisting that his contributions were vital to the Order's success. Atrius still distrusted him and pointed out that the events on Iokath gained the Alliance a powerful ally, whose support was now denied to the Order. Theron pretended to understand his concerns and asked for a way to prove his intentions, for which Atrius asked him to secure a shipment of [[Adegan crystal/Legends|adegan crystals]] from [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]].<ref name="Nathema" /> The [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] were transported on a [[Hovertrain/Legends|hovertrain]] headed to the [[Umbaran capital city/Legends|Umbara capital city]] and were guarded by [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] soldiers and [[Umbaran Shadow Assassin|Shadow Assassins]]. Theron arranged for a transmission from the [[Train/Legends|train]] to be send with the same encryption algorithm that was used on Iokath, tipping the [[Alliance Intelligence (Eternal Alliance)|Alliance Intelligence]] about the traitor's whereabouts.<ref name="Umbara" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_on_Umbara.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan on Umbara.]]
Theron was delivering to Commander a status report regarding the ongoing battle for Iokath and the search for the traitor when Lana approached them with the intel regarding Umbara. The three of them traveled to the shadow world in a shuttle and [[Crisis on Umbara|boarded the train]] to intercept and apprehend the traitor. After dealing with the opposing forces, they reached the empty cockpit of the train, where to the others' shock Theron showed himself to be the traitor. He fired a shot at Commander which hit Lana instead and another at the control panel which activated a [[Force field/Legends|force field]], trapping Lana and Commander inside the cabin.<ref name="Umbara" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_receives_the_message.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan during his time in the Order of Zildrog.]]
Theron then laid out his fake motivation, presenting himself as seeking the Alliance's downfall ever since the death of Valkorion in order to finally bring peace to the galaxy. Saying goodbye to Commander, Theron detonated charges on several train rings, causing the train to collide with a nearby mountain range, and escaped on a speeder bike. The Commander and Lana bailed out before the crash and survived just as he expected, and Theron quickly contacted them again, boasting how the delay would buy him enough time to get off-world with the adegan crystals. They chased after Theron and caught up with him just as his shuttle took off, leaving them to contend with an [[Umbaran Spider Tank]] which covered his escape.<ref name="Umbara" />

====Search for the holomap====
{{Quote|There it is. Of all the planets in the galaxy...|Theron learns of Zildrog's location on Nathema|<ref name="Copero">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|A Traitor Among the Chiss}}</ref>}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_on_Copero.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan on Copero.]]
Impressed with Theron's dedication to their cause, Atrius and the others reached a decision to welcome him into the Order of [[Zildrog]].<ref name="Umbara" /> Using his unique infiltration skills, Theron was tasked with finding a [[Holomap/Legends|holomap]] with coordinates to Zildrog's location and received specifications for it that he passed to [[Pova]], a spy operating on Nar Shaddaa. Pova was able to match the specs to a device stolen by [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] agents from the Sith Emperor decades ago as a collateral in case their deal with the Empire went south. The team was led by a [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force]] [[Zenta's grandfather|member]] of [[Inrokini family|House Inrokini]], whose granddaughter [[Zenta]] was now the [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]] of the House on [[Copero/Legends|Copero]].<ref name="Chasing Copero">{{TORweb|url=info/news/news-article/20171116|text="Chasing Copero"|int=Chasing Copero}}</ref> Having his lead, Theron headed to Copero and convinced Zenta to provide him refuge in exchange for providing her Alliance secrets. Zenta's brother [[Valss]] was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] and received a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of Theron's victory, which led him and several of Zenta's best fighters to join his cause. Theron sliced into Zenta's personal [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] to reveal the map's location and headed there with Valss and the others, abandoning the Syndic.<ref name="Copero" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_leaves_a_message.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan leaves a message for the Alliance.]]
Theron and Valss found the holomap in the [[Ancient ruins (Copero)|ancient ruins]] and activated it, revealing that [[Zildrog]] was located on [[Nathema]], to Theron's surprise. They then destroyed the map to cover their tracks and prepared to leave, when the Commander arrived to apprehend Theron, having received his location from Zenta. Valss rushed to engage them to buy Theron time to escape, despite his protests, and perished while Theron departed in a Zakuulan shuttle. Later, Theron transmitted the coordinates to Atrius, while intentionally leaving the channel between them open so that the Alliance could intercept their talk and learn of the Order's existence.<ref name="Copero" /> Having Zildrog's location, the Order moved its base of operations to Nathema, taking everything they could from the [[Abandoned listening post|Abandoned Listening Post]] that served as their previous base of operations. Theron was tasked with wiping all data and destroying the non-movable equipment, but instead he left encrypted backups of the data and leaked a message with the word "Zildrog" to the Alliance. As intended, it was intercepted by Lana and the Commander and Lana, who personally investigated the [[Listening post/Legends|listening post]] and found his message with a set of coordinates on Nathema that was encrypted with a unique method that Theron and Lana developed together on Rishi.<ref name="Nathema" />

====Endgame on Nathema====
{{Quote|I stalled them with false data for as long as I could, but we don't have much time. If we act now, we can stop the Order before they activate Zildrog.|Theron Shan|<ref name="Nathema" />}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_on_Nathema.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan on Nathema]]
On Nathema, the Order uncovered Zildrog and began the preparations for the ritual needed to awaken it, while Theron slipped away and waited at his coordinates. When Lana and the Commander [[Mission to Nathema (Zildrog)|arrived as predicted]], Theron revealed himself and laid down his weapon, explaining the situation and apologizing for the necessary deception. Though Lana still did not fully trust him, everyone agreed that the Order should be stopped, and Theron led her and the Commander towards the [[Emperor's Vaults|Emperor's Vault]] under an ancient [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]], where Zildrog was located. Along the way, Theron apologized to Lana for deceiving her, reminding of the time she had similarly kept him in the dark on Rishi.<ref name="Nathema" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_backstabbed_by_Vinn_Atrius.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Theron Shan is backstabbed by Vinn Atrius.]]
The three of them reached the Emperor's Vault, where Vinn Atrius and GEMINI 16 were already in the process of awakening Zildrog, and Theron immediately shot Atrius. GEMINI 16 then trapped them in a [[Force field/Legends|force field]] and revealed that Zildrog was already awakened, while Zildrog then used his connection to the [[Dark Sanctuary]] to remotely take over the ''Gravestone'' which remained parked on Odessen. Zildrog took the ''Gravestone'' into Odessen's orbit and proceeded to repeatedly fire the omnicannon at the Eternal Fleet, which sat defenseless in the absence of orders from the Eternal Throne. Theron, Lana and the Commander were unable to do anything to stop Zildrog from annihilating the entire Eternal Fleet. Zildrog then targeted Odessen itself and began to recharge before the next attack, dropping the force field and giving them an opening to engage GEMINI 16 directly.

[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Lana_Beniko_on_Nathema.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Forgiven by the Commander, Theron was allowed to rejoin the Alliance.]]
Theron, Lana and the Commander battled and destroyed the GEMINI droid, after which Theron attempted to shut Zildrog down, but was suddenly stabbed in the back with a [[Lightsaber pike/Legends|lightsaber pike]] by Vinn Atrius. Lana and Commander defeated Atrius and destroyed Zildrog, but the last act also triggered the self-destruct of the ''Gravestone'' and disabled the Eternal Throne. The Commander decided Atrius' fate while Lana tended to Theron's wounds, determining that he needed immediate treatment. The Commander ordered to bring Theron home to Odessen, where after some time he became strong enough to walk and approached Lana and Commander in the hangar. He apologized for his actions and asked for forgiveness, after which the Commander welcomed him back, and Lana ensured that the three of them would face any future challenges together.<ref name="Nathema" />

===New Galactic Conflict===
====Invasion of Ossus====
Later in [[3628 BBY]],<ref name="TOR Dates Forums">{{TOR_updates|5.10}}</ref> when a [[Third Galactic War|new conflict]] between the Sith Empire and Republic erupted with an [[Invasion of Ossus|invasion]] of a [[Jedi Colony]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], the Commander joined the Republic's side in aiding and defending the colony. However, Theron decided to remain behind on Odessen, as the mission called for the Commander to head in alone.<ref name="TOR510">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Inflection Point|[[Odessen]]}}</ref>

[[File:Theron_back_with_Alliance.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan is back with the Eternal Alliance.]]
The [[3627 BBY|following year]],<ref name="3627 Date">{{TOR_updates|5.10.3}}</ref> Theron attended a meeting between the Alliance Commander and the various leaders of the Alliance, including [[Juvard Illip Oggurobb|Doctor Oggurobb]], [[Hylo Visz]], [[Bey'wan Aygo]], [[Lana Beniko]], and [[Koth Vortena]]. During the meeting, Theron informed the Commander that his assets were bringing in solid information about major battles all along the front lines, and that he was forwarding all of it to [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] Aygo so that he could analyze and predict strategic probabilities going forward. After the meeting concluded, Theron took the Commander aside for a moment alone and expressed that he felt good about working with the Republic again, and that he was glad to be a part of it.<ref name="HeartsAndMinds">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Hearts and Minds|[[Odessen]]}}</ref>

====Mission to Onderon====
{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_on_Onderon.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan on Onderon]]
Later in the year, when the Commander was tasked with heading to [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] with [[Arn Peralun]] in order to ensure the safety of the [[Eleventh Fleet (Galactic Republic)|Republic fleet]] refueling in orbit, Theron Shan assisted Lana Beniko with determining the plans of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Regalun Petryph|Petryph]], discovering that he intended to strip-mine Onderon to line his pockets.<ref name="PalaceIntrigue">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Palace Intrigue|Onderon}}</ref>

Once the Commander was able to determine the position of [[Darth Savik]], the Sith sent to Onderon to ensure the destruction of the Republic Fleet refueling above it, Theron was able to set up a [[Sensor/Legends|sensor lock]] around the area where Savik had fled to, ensuring that, if she tried to leave, she wouldn't have been able to without being discovered. Almost immediately, the sensors began picking up energy blooms, which Theron theorized might be the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]] powering up.<ref name="LightOfDiplomacy">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|The Light of Diplomacy|Onderon}}</ref>

After the Commander was able to capture Savik, Theron and Lana explained that they had loaded her up onto an [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]] shuttle, and that, while Savik wished to stay with the Alliance Commander, the Republic was requesting for her to be transferred over to their control. They left the decision of who would get Savik up to the Commander.<ref name="SpringingTrap">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Springing the Trap|Onderon}}</ref>

====Mission to Mek-Sha====
Theron, alongside Lana Beniko, accompanied the Commander to [[Mek-Sha]] in order to ensure that the [[Twenty-Ninth Fleet]] commanded by [[Vice Admiral/Legends|Vice Admiral]] [[Dol Narlock]] would be able to refuel safely. While the Commander was meeting with Narlock and [[Junker Jott]], Theron and Lana mentioned to [[Hylo Visz]] and [[Gault Rennow]] that they were on Mek-Sha.<ref name="GangsOfMekSha">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|The Gangs of Mek-Sha|Mek-Sha}}</ref>

[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Lana_Beniko_on_Mek-Sha.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron and Lana on Mek-Sha]]
Following the Empire's assault on Mek-Sha's docks, Lana informed the commander that [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ardinondu Dipolus Daeruun|Daeruun]] had sent coordinates to a strategy meeting on how best to defend Corellia, and had strictly instructed them that only the Commander was to attend. Theron jokingly commented on the orders, saying that he couldn't imagine why the General would be uncomfortable sharing battle plans with either him or Lana.<ref name="DefendingTheDocks">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Defending the Docks|Mek-Sha}}</ref>

====Defending the Meridian Complex====
During the defense of the Meridian Complex, Theron Shan was placed in a ground team that was looking to subtley sneak through the enemy lines. He stated to the Commander and General Daeruun that saying exactly what he was doing over [[Comlink/Legends|comms]] would ultimately defeat the purpose. When Lana and [[Aric Jorgan]] encountered a large number of Imperial reinforcements, Theron moved to help them hold their position, telling the Commander to keep moving. Some of the reinforcements got past them, however, but were then intercepted by Gnost-Dural and Daeruun.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=flashpoint|Objective: Meridian}}</ref>

[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Lana_Beniko_on_Carrick_Station.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron and Lana discuss joining the Republic.]]
Following the defense of the complex, and the transformation of the Alliance into [[Task Force Nova]], Theron and Lana spoke with the Commander aboard [[Carrick Station]]. Lana expressed her thoughts that fitting in with the Republic and the Jedi would be an interesting situation for her, but admitted that Gnost-Dural seemed open-minded enough, to which Theron stated that he'd told her that Gnost-Dural was alright. Lana then changed the subject, suggesting that she, Theron, and the Commander stop by the cantina, as a general was offering free drinks to anyone with an impressive Corellia story. Before they could, however, [[Tau Idair]] and Arn Peralun took the Commander aside for a brief conversation, to which Theron and Lana obliged before departing.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian" />

====Tenebrae's Final Weapon====
[[File:Theron_Shan_in_Echoes_of_Oblivion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan insists on accompanying Commander on the mission.]]
In [[3626 BBY]],<ref name="Dates6.2">{{TOR_updates|6.2}}</ref> [[T7-O1]] discovered the location of the [[Kira Carsen's ship|vessel]] that [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] and [[Kira Carsen]] had placed [[Satele Shan]] and her students aboard after it had been momentarily lost. The Alliance Commander, alongside Carsen and Scourge, prepared to set out to deal with the situation, as onboard the ship, [[Tenebrae]]'s [[Tenebrae's curse|final weapon]] was getting stronger by the minute. However, just before they departed, and after the Commander had spoken with Lana, Theron told the Commander that he was going with them. When the Commander told him that it would be too dangerous for him to come along, he insisted that he must, as it was a matter concerning his mother. Adding on to that, he assured the Commander that whatever the Emperor was doing, he would be able to resist it, as he had done on [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]]. Ultimately, the Commander allowed him, as well as [[Senya Tirall]] and [[Arcann]] to come, with Theron stating that the only orders he followed were the Commander's when Carsen and Scourge raised objections.

Once onboard the ship, Theron reconvened with the Commander and the rest on the Medical Deck, where they fought and defeated [[Servant Four]]. When the time came for Kira Carsen to lead the group in meditation to enter [[Mindscape|Satele's mind]], however, Theron expressed that he didn't wish to see the inside of his mother's mind, and instead remained on guard while the rest delved in.

Following Tenebrae's ultimate and final defeat, Theron assisted Kira and Scourge in transporting Satele's surviving students to their [[Jedi Temple/Legends|old training grounds]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Meanwhile, Satele pulled the Commander into a private talk within her mind. While there, she thanked the Commander for giving Theron a home he always needed, as he had now finally found a place of belonging that she could not give to him.<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Echoes of Oblivion|Odessen}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Jedi Grand Master mom, Supreme Commander dad. Now we get why Theron's so messed up.|Teff'ith|<ref name="Annihilation" />}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_talks_to_Beywan_Aygo.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan was an expert spy with many years of experience.]]
Theron had a difficult family life, not knowing who his father was until well into adulthood.<ref name="Annihilation" /> Though he knew that his mother was the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the Jedi Order, he was raised since infancy by her master [[Ngani Zho]] and the two never even acknowledged their relationship during their early encounters.<ref name="Lost Suns 05" /> Theron faced another blow from fate, when he was discovered not to be Force-sensitive and abandoned by Master Zho as well,<ref name="Lost Suns 01" /> though he later remarked that things turned out surprisingly well for him.<ref name="FAI" /> Theron was a loyal Republic patriot, refusing to entertained either a notion of defecting when offered by [[Darth Mekhis]]<ref name="Lost Suns 05" /> and almost instantly suspecting [[Rian Darok]] of working against the Republic.<ref name="FAI" />

[[File:Theron_and_Lana_after_victory.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Theron Shan had a long working relationship with Lana Beniko.]]
Theron formed an odd relationship with [[Lana Beniko]], which since their first meeting on Manaan progressed between caution,<ref name="FAII" /> open distrust,<ref name="Frontal Assault" /> reluctant cooperation,<ref name="Dead Center" /> almost complete trust,<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> and eventually a (faked) betrayal.<ref name="Umbara" /> Following the destruction of the ''[[Ascendant Spear]]'', Theron was able to have some sort of semi-professional relationship with his parents, who neither really became close to him.<ref name="Annihilation" /> His mistakes on [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], which claimed the lives of almost all [[Sixth Line]] Jedi and led to the Republic invasion weighted on him hard.<ref name="The End of It All" />

[[File:Theron_Shans_new_look.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan changes with visual appearance while undercover in the Order of Zildrog.]]
Theron never trusted the Republic Chancellor [[Leontyne Saresh]], feeling betrayed when [[Rane Kovach]] was revealed to be working for her<ref name="The End of It All" /> and approving the punishment [[Alliance Commander|the Commander]] gave to her on [[Odessen]].<ref name="KOTETChapter2" /> It was Saresh's policy that caused Theron to abandon the Republic and join the Alliance,<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> which cost him whatever relationship he had with his father.<ref name="The Forgotten World" /> In the Alliance Theron worked on problems from every angle, to the point that even Lana suggested he take more rest.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> During his initial team-up with Lana he was constantly wary of the Empire, favoring sabotage, distrust, and abuse of the momentary truce to further Republic interests.<ref name="Confederacy" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_is_forgiven.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Theron was eventually forgiven for his betrayal by the Commander.]]
By the time he joined the Alliance five years later, he became more soft and almost never weighted towards more cruel actions.<ref name="KOTFEChapter16" /> Theron's routine included daily calibration of his cybernetic implants, reading aid requests and managing Alliance crisis reports. SIS training resulted in him being hyper-alert and constantly scanning his surroundings for possible threats. Theron's drinks of choice included morning [[Caf/Legends|caf]] to wake up and [[Whiskey/Legends|whiskey]] that helped him sleep.<ref>{{TORcite|type=message|Surveillance Report: Theron Shan|The Monitors}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Theron_shan.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan concept art by [[Chris Anderson (artist)|Chris Anderson]]]]
Theron Shan was first mentioned indirectly in [[the Holonet]] section of the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' website, which included the phrase "a secret son" written in [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] next to [[Satele Shan]]. His name was later revealed in the [[Star Wars Insider 124|124th issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine. Theron Shan first appeared in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series [[Star Wars: The Old Republic — The Lost Suns|''Star Wars: The Old Republic—The Lost Suns'']], released in [[2011]] and set around the same time as ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' video game.<ref name="Lost Suns 01" /> He later appeared in the [[2012]] novel ''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]'', set between the events of the original game and its first expansion ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''. [[Drew Karpyshyn]], author of ''Annihilation'', responded to a question via Twitter that Theron Shan was 30 during the events of the novel, meaning that Shan was born in [[3670 BBY]]. However, the novel itself stated that Shan was conceived after the Battle of Alderaan, which occurred in [[3667 BBY]].<ref name="Annihilation" />

Theron Shan was later added to the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' video game itself, first appearing during the ''Forged Alliances'' storyline, released in April [[2014]]. In the game he is voiced by [[Troy Baker]], who also provided voice for [[Jedi Consular]] companion [[Zenith]].<ref name="FAI" /> Theron played a significant role in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan|''Shadow of Revan'']], [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] and [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']] expansions, being one of the most prominent NPC in the game alongside [[Lana Beniko]]. Theron becomes available as a companion after the completion of ''Fallen Empire'' '''Chapter IX: The Alliance'''.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> He also appears in several short stories released on the game's official website.

[[File:Steam_Trading_Cards_Theron_Shan.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Theron Shan]]
Theron is portrayed as bisexual; male and female player characters have the option to flirt with him during the ''Forged Alliances'' and [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan|''Shadow of Revan'']] storyline. The outcome of the flirtation depends on the player's faction, leading to a kiss with Imperial characters on Yavin IV or a kiss and fade to black for Republic characters.<ref name="The Enemy Within" /> During ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter IX players will have an option to flirt with him regardless of past choices, after which they can initially a full romance with either Theron, [[Lana Beniko]] or [[Koth Vortena]].<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> If they player chooses Theron, there will be a number of additional romance dialogue and cutscenes present during both ''Fallen Empire'' and ''Eternal Throne'' expansions. When their original romanced companion returns, players can choose to resume that romance, which leads to a break-up with Theron. During the betrayal on Umbara player can ask if their relationship was just a lie; Theron will respond that he is indeed in love with the player, but the Eternal Alliance needs to be stopped regardless. At the end of Nathema flashpoints, Theron will propose to formally [[Marriage/Legends|marry]] the player.<ref name="Nathema" />

===Gameplay alternatives===
*During the ''Legacy of the Rakata'' flashpoint, Theron will ask Republic players to overload a console to deny [[Infinite Army]] knowledge to the Empire, while also killing cyborgs in their sleep. Players can refuse for Light Side points, in which case Theron will protest that it is not the time to take chances, while the player had to kill the cyborgs anyway.<ref name="Legacy of the Rakata">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=flashpoint|Legacy of the Rakata}}</ref>

*On [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] Theron will ask Republic players to modify the sensor equipment to allowed the Republic to spy on the Imperial allies. Players can agree with him for Dark Side points or refuse for Light Side points.<ref name="Confederacy" />

*At the end of the [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] storyline, players can either allow Theron to take Master [[Surro]] to [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] for healing as a Light Side option, let Lana take her for experiments as a Dark Side option or kill Surro on the spot, angering them both.<ref name="Dead Center" /> Players can also guilt him into quitting SIS after the fiasco that he caused for Dark Side points.<ref name="The End of It All" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_in_cuffs.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Koth Vortena's crew put Theron Shan in cuffs.]]
*During ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter XV, Theron will become angry if the player lets [[Tai Cordan]] die in favor of saving [[Malita Tal]] and [[Zasha Ranken]].<ref name="KOTFEChapter15" />

*During ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter XVI, if the player previously alienated [[Koth Vortena]] into abandoning the Alliance, he will return and steal the ''Gravestone'' after the [[Battle of Odessen]], putting Theron and [[Tora]] in [[Binders/Legends|binders]] and ejecting them in an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]]. If the player chose to open fire on [[Arcann]]'s shuttle, Theron will criticize them, as this put [[Senya Tirall]] in danger as well.<ref name="KOTFEChapter16" />

*During ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter II, player can either lock [[Leontyne Saresh]] in the Alliance prison, or execute her on the spot, with Theron equally approving on both actions.<ref name="KOTETChapter2" />

[[File:Theron_and_Lana_replace_Arcann_and_Senya.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Theron and Lana replace Arcann and Senya.]]
*In ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter VIII, if the player previously made Dark Side choices that resulted in [[Senya Tirall]] and [[Arcann]] being killed, Theron and Lana will accompany them through the battle instead, including the fight against Vaylin.<ref name="KOTETChapter8" />

*During ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter IX, if Senya and Arcann were previously killed, Theron and Lana will accompany the player to the [[Eternal Throne]] instead. They will hold off the [[Skytrooper]]s as the player fights Valkorion in their mind, sharing a tender moment when they believe they are making their last stand.<ref name="KOTETChapter9" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_watches_Jace_Malcom_die.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron Shan mourns the death of his father on Iokath.]]
*During the [[War on Iokath]], player must side with either the Empire or the Republic, possibly against the original faction, neither of which is a Light or Dark side choice. If the player sides with the Republic, Theron will once again work alongside his father [[Jace Malcom]] for the good of the Republic. If the player sides with the Empire however, Malcom will disavow his son and Theron will be forced to formulate a plan on how to beat him. In this scenario, Malcom will assume a Throne on Iokath despite Theron's pleas, which will mortally injure him. Malcom will die in his son's arms, asking Theron to tell Satele that he was sorry. Later, Lana will ask for permission to independently spy on every [[Eternal Alliance]] member, herself and Theron included, to which Theron will oppose as a paranoid overreaction. Players can either agree with Theron in a Light Side option or allow Lana to proceed in a Dark Side option.<ref name="Showdown" />

*During the "[[Crisis on Umbara]]" flashpoint, Theron will say that either the Alliance outgrew the player if they previously claimed the [[Eternal Throne]] as a peacekeeper or claim that the player is now a tyrant if they claimed the Throne as a new Emperor. During the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] address, players can either pledge one hundred [[Eternal Fleet warship]]s as a peacekeeping force under Theron's command, asking him to come back home in a Light Side option, or declare him a terrorist and a madman, placing one billion credit bounty on his head in a Dark Side option.<ref name="Umbara" />

[[File:Death_of_Theron_Shan.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The death of Theron Shan]]
*During "The Nathema Conspiracy" flashpoint, players can choose to leave Theron to die on Nathema in a Dark Side option. If they make the Light Side option to take him back to Odessen instead, there will be a neutral choice to welcome him back or permanently banish him from the Alliance.<ref name="Nathema" />

*During the "Objective: Meridian" flashpoint, if the player had sided the Alliance with the Sith Empire, the player can choose the Light Side option to convince [[Darth Krovos]] to avoid civilian casualties on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], resulting in Theron agreeing to give the Empire a chance. Alternatively, if the player supported Krovos' indiscriminate bombardment of the planet, Theron will state as much as he wants to trust the player, he feels that the Sith cannot be trusted. If the player is a saboteur for the Republic but did not stop Krovos, Theron will state that there's no point in tearing the Empire from the inside if he/she is not going to protect civilians. If the player had sided the Alliance with the Republic but is a saboteur for the Empire, Theron will label the Imperials who bombed civilians on Corellia as monsters. He will state that he trusts the Commander to make the right choices, but he doesn't know whether he can trust the Sith.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian" />

*During the "Echoes of Oblivion" flashpoint, Theron will ask the Commander to allow him to come along and help his mother. He will accompany the Commander regardless of their choice. If Arcann and Senya were previously saved on Voss, Theron will accompany them in their shuttle and Arcann will distract the Servants firing upon the Commander's shuttle. If the player chose to kill Arcann and Senya as a dark side option, Theron will pilot the other Shuttle himself and will distract the Servants. If however, Theron was either killed or banished from the Alliance, and Arcann and Senya are also dead, their role will be played by Lana instead.<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion" />

If the player starts an Imperial class using a Commander's Token, thus skipping the preceding story quests, it will assume dark side choices had always been selected. The only exception to this is Theron's role in the Nathema Conspiracy, with Theron being welcomed back into the alliance on that account.<ref name="Onslaught" />
